newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks score record close but end off peaks.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks score record close but end off peaks.

text.p: Banking stocks led a broad rally in Hong Kong share prices on Monday, with the Hang Seng Index hitting a record high in morning trade before ending the day off its peaks as property stocks succumbed to profit-taking.

The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 145.65 points, or 0.96 percent, at a record closing high of 15,370.94 after hitting an all-time high of 15,502.54 in early trade. Turnover was HK$19.07 billion compared with HK$18.55 billion on Friday.
"Local short-term liquidity and momentum pushed the market up this morning," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.
"But property stocks came off, leading the index down."

Speculation that Chinese firms would continue buying into Hong Kong companies also boosted prices, particularly in the banking sector after red chip COSCO Pacific Ltd said it planned to raise its stake in Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd.
"Second-line finance stocks are really beginning to boom," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
Among the biggest gainers of the session, Wing Hang Bank Ltd rose HK$5.00 to HK$47.50, Wing Lung Bank Ltd added HK$1.20 to HK$50.00 and Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd advanced HK$1.15 to HK$19.90.
Blue chips like Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd which rose HK$1.40 to HK$31.50, and Hopewell Holdings Ltd, up HK$0.15 to HK$5.10, also benefited from the speculation.
"Investors think some blue chips have the potential to be acquired by red chips," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.

HSBC Holdings Plc roared to a record high of HK$250.00 before closing the session up HK$4.00 at HK$249.00 as investors hoped for strong results ahead of the company's interim announcement on August 4.

In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd closed on a loss of HK$0.25 at HK$92.25 after rising to a high of HK$94.50. Henderson Land Development Co Ltd closed down HK$0.25 at HK$69.25 after hitting a high of HK$70.50.

"Property stocks rallied in morning trade because they had slumped to good value, but to move to a new high they need something to push them up," said Tam. "They will have to wait until the government announces its property measures."
Remington said the Hang Seng Index had hit resistance around 15,500. "We need some news to push it through. It could go down tomorrow," he said.
